prompt: In 120 to 180 words, explain threshold selection for a risk model in exactly five numbered points. Include costs, calibration, validation, and finish with a one-sentence conclusion.

turns.user_message: In 120 to 180 words, explain threshold selection for a risk model in exactly five numbered points. Include costs, calibration, validation, and finish with a one-sentence conclusion.
turns.assistant_message: Threshold selection in a risk model balances sensitivity and specificity based on real-world implications. First, define the cost of false positives versus false negatives — e.g., in healthcare, missing a disease (false negative) may cost more than unnecessary testing (false positive). Second, use the ROC curve to identify thresholds where the trade-off between true positive rate and false positive rate aligns with these cost ratios. Third, apply cost-benefit analysis: calculate expected loss at each threshold using prevalence, costs, and probabilities to minimize total expected cost. Fourth, validate the selected threshold on an independent dataset to ensure performance generalizes beyond training data and avoids overfitting. Fifth, calibrate model outputs so predicted probabilities reflect true observed frequencies — miscalibrated models yield misleading thresholds even if discrimination is strong. The optimal threshold minimizes expected cost while maintaining model reliability and clinical or operational utility.
